pinboard.title: Opinion | I Am a Silicon Valley Veteran. We Are Sabotaging Ourselves. - The New York Times
pinboard.description:
By Jaron Lanier
There are better alternatives to agents. I do research into complex new manufacturing and materials technology using large A.I. models. In the course of my efforts, I am pelted with pop-ups to launch agents, but I have realized they are not so effective because I have to constantly backpedal when I get results that aren’t quite right — unless I give in and accept what comes easy to the agent. (This is how A.I. slop happens.) Instead, I am starting to use a process I call Mind Gliders, where I use the newest models to create a custom, single-use editor for the general zone of ideas I want to research at that moment, and then explore possibilities using sliders on my screen until I have zeroed in on what I was trying to create.

pinboard.title: Fable 5.2 One-Shotted My Nephew's Dream Game
pinboard.description:
LLMs can make complete multi-level games that are fun.

TL;DR - Fable 5.2 one-shotted my nephew's dream game from a bunch of drawings, and it's a lot of fun. You can try it here.

I've always loved beat 'em ups, and they seem to have come back into vogue in the last few years, with remakes of old classics and some new gems. When my nephews visit, I use it as an excuse to try them out.

Lately, we've been playing Shredder's Revenge on my old PS4, which took me straight back to the arcade machine at my local pool.

One day, my younger nephew, Aiden, came to me with a proposal. Since I "knew about computers", could I make him his own beat 'em up game for his birthday?

He had already drawn up the game design docs. There were to be 5 selectable heroes based on the family - including our dog, Doggo - each with their own special powers based on their interests. He had 12 bosses drawn up and a loose outline of a story. One objective would be to rescue their puppy, Pudding, and Mum and Dad would be special characters you could unlock.

I owe my family and all of you an apology.

I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.

Throughout my life, my family has given me love and support. They deserve my honesty and loyalty. Instead, I let them down and damaged the life we built together. I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused, and I accept the criticism that comes with it.

To my wife and family: I love you. I know an apology cannot undo what I have done. I hope our family will heal and that, over time, I can earn back your trust. 

To my colleagues at NVIDIA, including those I have worked alongside for decades, and to our board, partners, and shareholders around the world: you deserve better from me. Leading NVIDIA is the privilege of my life. My responsibility is to serve you and be worthy of your trust. I have fallen short of that responsibility. I am fully committed to NVIDIA and will work to earn back your confidence.

Regarding the national security concerns raised in news reports, NVIDIA’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American.

My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy.

Jensen

pinboard.title: AI is history | Brendan Keogh
pinboard.description: But I’m always deeply suspicious of any attempt to situate a technology outside of history. My whole academic career to date has, in part, been about resisting narratives of videogames as magically totally different from every media form that came before them. I am likewise skeptical that generative AI represents a profound cut from history. That somehow, unlike every previous contradictory technological innovation of the past couple centuries of capitalism, generative AI is just simply ‘evil’. Instead, I would suggest it represents the same profound contradictions of technological innovation under capitalism as all the previous ones, just now on an even larger scale. The potentially useful byproducts are larger, as is the possible profits that are the actual goal and the undeniable harms.

pinboard.title: India’s App Economy in 18 Charts - by Manish Singh
pinboard.description:
he apps at the top of Indian phones have barely changed in nearly three years, but much of the market beneath them has reshuffled, according to an India Dispatch analysis of Sensor Tower data.

AI chatbots have gone mainstream, and ChatGPT, which had little traction in early 2024, now has nearly as many users in India as Telegram. In ride-hailing and online shopping, challengers have drawn more users than the incumbents. Netflix and Spotify have gained users while most of their rivals, including Amazon Prime Video and JioSaavn, have shrunk. Quick commerce app Blinkit has grown several times over, and short-drama apps that barely registered in early 2024 now have more than 100 million users between them.
